title: Non-monotonic dependence of OAM Schmidt spectrum on crystal thickness
authors: Harshal Jain, Suman Karan, Radhika Prasad, Anand K. Jha
abstract: The orbital angular momentum (OAM) of photons provides a high-dimensional resource for quantum information protocols. The dimensionality of OAM-entangled states generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is quantified by the angular Schmidt spectrum. Here, we experimentally investigate the dependence of the angular Schmidt spectrum on the thickness of the nonlinear crystal. Contrary to previous studies reporting a monotonic decrease in the Schmidt number with increasing crystal thickness, we report the first experimental observation of a nonmonotonic behavior, as we demonstrate an increase in the Schmidt number beyond a certain crystal thickness. We attribute this to the spatial walk-off effect in the anisotropic nonlinear crystal and explain it using a theoretical model that is devoid of standard phase-matching approximations. These findings can have important implications for high-dimensional entangled state generation.
summary: The paper experimentally and theoretically investigates how crystal thickness affects the dimensionality (Schmidt number) of OAM-entangled photon pairs generated via SPDC. The key finding is the first observation of non-monotonic behavior, which arises from spatial walk-off effects in anisotropic crystals. This work emphasizes that using the full phase-matching theory, rather than approximations, is essential for accurate quantum state characterization.
main_problem: The study investigates how the dimensionality of orbital angular momentum (OAM) entangled states, quantified by the Schmidt number, changes as a function of nonlinear crystal thickness.
main_result: Contrary to previous predictions, the authors experimentally and theoretically demonstrate that the Schmidt number exhibits non-monotonic behavior—increasing after an initial decrease—due to spatial walk-off effects in anisotropic crystals.
method: The work combines experimental measurements using SPDC with theoretical modeling that incorporates the full phase-matching function, explicitly accounting for spatial walk-off terms neglected in prior approximations.
model_or_system: The system involves generating OAM-entangled photon pairs via Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion (SPDC) within an anisotropic nonlinear crystal like BBO. The state is analyzed using the Schmidt decomposition formalism.
key_observables: Angular Schmidt spectrum ($S_l$) and the associated Schmidt number ($K$).
important_parameters: Crystal thickness ($L$), phase-matching angle ($	heta_p$), and the spatial walk-off term ($\Delta k_{	ext{extra}}^z$).
main_assumptions: The primary limitation addressed is the failure of previous theoretical models that used approximate phase-matching conditions by neglecting spatial walk-off.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the Schmidt number dependence on thickness, showing a monotonic decrease (approximate) versus a non-monotonic increase (exact/experimental). Appendix figures compare zero-radial-mode spectra using both approximate and exact formulations, highlighting divergence at larger thicknesses.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework for OAM entanglement via SPDC. It then contrasts previous approximate models with the full model incorporating spatial walk-off. The core of the work presents experimental measurements confirming the non-monotonic trend predicted by the exact theory, followed by detailed comparisons of spectral convergence across different approximations.
why_interesting: This research provides a crucial refinement to the theoretical understanding of high-dimensional quantum state generation in optics, showing that neglecting geometric effects like walk-off can lead to fundamentally incorrect predictions about entanglement resource scaling with device size.
